origins.name: Origins
origins.blurb: The first digital images, and a new question: can a machine see?

classical.name: Classical vision
classical.blurb: Geometry, physics and mathematics, designed by hand one step at a time.

features.name: Features & machine learning
features.blurb: Hand-crafted features plus statistical classifiers take vision out of the lab.

deep.name: Big data & deep learning
deep.blurb: ImageNet and GPUs make deep neural networks the default method.

transformer.name: Transformers & multimodality
transformer.blurb: Attention replaces convolution; images and language share one space.

generative.name: Generation & foundation models
generative.blurb: Image, video and 3D generation, and foundation models shared across tasks.

firstDigitalImage.title: The first digital image
firstDigitalImage.summary: Russell Kirsch used the SEAC computer at the US National Bureau of Standards to scan a photo of his son into a 176×176 pixel grid.
firstDigitalImage.impact: For the first time an image existed in computer memory as numbers, the precondition for all later image processing.

perceptron.title: Rosenblatt's perceptron
perceptron.summary: Frank Rosenblatt described the perceptron, a single-layer neural network that learned to classify simple visual patterns from data.
perceptron.impact: The idea of a machine that learns from examples instead of being programmed, the distant root of today's deep learning.

visualCortex.title: Simple and complex cells in the visual cortex
visualCortex.summary: Hubel and Wiesel recorded cells in the cat visual cortex that fire only for edges at a specific orientation, organised in layers.
visualCortex.impact: Layered receptive fields became the direct inspiration for convolutional networks.

houghTransform.title: The Hough transform
houghTransform.summary: Paul Hough patented a way to find straight lines in bubble-chamber photos by letting each pixel vote in a parameter space.
houghTransform.impact: Voting in parameter space is still how lines, circles and road lanes are found in images.

blocksWorld.title: Blocks world
blocksWorld.summary: Larry Roberts' MIT thesis recovered three-dimensional shape from a single two-dimensional photo of polyhedral blocks.
blocksWorld.impact: The foundation of 3D vision: inferring an object's geometry from a flat image.

fastFourierTransform.title: The fast Fourier transform (FFT)
fastFourierTransform.summary: Cooley and Tukey published the FFT, cutting the cost of frequency analysis of signals and images from quadratic to near-linear.
fastFourierTransform.impact: Made frequency-domain filtering, image compression and fast convolution practical on computers.

summerVisionProject.title: The MIT Summer Vision Project
summerVisionProject.summary: Seymour Papert set a group of students the goal of solving segmentation and object recognition over a single summer.
summerVisionProject.impact: A classic lesson: vision is far harder than human intuition suggests.

shapeFromShading.title: Shape from shading
shapeFromShading.summary: Berthold Horn's MIT thesis recovered the three-dimensional shape of a surface from the shading in a single image.
shapeFromShading.impact: Opened the "shape from X" family of problems, from shading and texture to today's depth estimation.

otsuThreshold.title: Otsu thresholding
otsuThreshold.summary: Nobuyuki Otsu chose the foreground/background threshold automatically by maximising the between-class variance of the histogram.
otsuThreshold.impact: The default way to binarise images in OCR, industrial inspection and medical imaging for over four decades.

neocognitron.title: Neocognitron
neocognitron.summary: Kunihiko Fukushima built a layered network of S-cells and C-cells modelled on the visual cortex, recognising handwriting regardless of position.
neocognitron.impact: The first convolution-and-downsampling architecture, the direct ancestor of the modern CNN.

marrHildreth.title: Marr–Hildreth edge detection
marrHildreth.summary: Marr and Hildreth located edges at zero crossings of the Laplacian of a Gaussian-smoothed image, at several scales.
marrHildreth.impact: Turned a theory of biological vision into an algorithm and seeded the idea of multi-scale image analysis.

opticalFlow.title: Optical flow
opticalFlow.summary: Horn and Schunck, alongside Lucas and Kanade, showed how to estimate per-pixel motion between two frames.
opticalFlow.impact: Still the basis of object tracking, image stabilisation and video analysis today.

ransac.title: RANSAC
ransac.summary: Fischler and Bolles fitted models by sampling a few points at random, counting how many agree, and keeping the model with the most support.
ransac.impact: The standard way to survive outliers in image stitching, camera calibration and 3D reconstruction.

generalizedHough.title: The generalised Hough transform
generalizedHough.summary: Dana Ballard extended the Hough transform to arbitrary shapes using a lookup table of edge-to-centre vectors.
generalizedHough.impact: One of the first shape-based object detectors; centre voting survives in modern detectors.

essentialMatrix.title: The essential matrix and the eight-point algorithm
essentialMatrix.summary: Longuet-Higgins showed that eight point correspondences between two images determine the relative camera motion and scene structure.
essentialMatrix.impact: The mathematical basis of two-view geometry, used in every structure-from-motion and SLAM system.

marrVision.title: David Marr's three levels of analysis
marrVision.summary: The book Vision proposed splitting the problem into computational, representation-and-algorithm, and implementation levels.
marrVision.impact: A framework that turned vision into a structured science rather than a collection of tricks.

scaleSpace.title: Scale-space theory
scaleSpace.summary: Witkin and Koenderink formalised looking at an image across a continuous range of Gaussian blurs, the scale space.
scaleSpace.impact: The theory behind scale-invariant features such as SIFT and behind feature-pyramid networks.

backpropagation.title: Backpropagation
backpropagation.summary: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularised backpropagation for training multi-layer neural networks.
backpropagation.impact: The same learning mechanism still sits underneath almost every vision model.

cannyEdges.title: The Canny edge detector
cannyEdges.summary: John Canny framed edge detection as an optimisation with three criteria: few errors, accurate localisation, and one response per edge.
cannyEdges.impact: A classic image-processing algorithm that ships in every vision library to this day.

tsaiCalibration.title: Tsai camera calibration
tsaiCalibration.summary: Roger Tsai gave an accurate calibration procedure, including lens distortion, for off-the-shelf cameras and lenses.
tsaiCalibration.impact: Brought camera-based 3D measurement into factories and industrial robots.

activeContours.title: Active contours (snakes)
activeContours.summary: Kass, Witkin and Terzopoulos modelled an object boundary as an elastic curve that deforms to lock onto image edges.
activeContours.impact: Started energy-based segmentation, long a workhorse of medical imaging.

harrisCorner.title: The Harris corner detector
harrisCorner.summary: Harris and Stephens detected corners from the local gradient matrix, points that are easy to find again across images.
harrisCorner.impact: The standard interest point for tracking and image matching for years, the precursor of later keypoint detectors.

convNetBackprop.title: Convolutional networks trained with backpropagation
convNetBackprop.summary: Yann LeCun and colleagues trained a convolutional network with backpropagation to read handwritten zip codes.
convNetBackprop.impact: The first time convolution, weight sharing and end-to-end learning came together: the recipe of the modern CNN.

eigenfaces.title: Eigenfaces
eigenfaces.summary: Turk and Pentland used principal component analysis to represent a face with a few dozen coefficients.
eigenfaces.impact: Face recognition that ran on ordinary computers, and an early move toward learning representations from data.

jpeg.title: The JPEG standard
jpeg.summary: JPEG applied the discrete cosine transform to 8×8 blocks plus quantisation to compress photos by a factor of ten or more.
jpeg.impact: Made digital images shareable everywhere, and created the web-scale photo collections later vision models learned from.

supportVectorMachines.title: Support vector machines
supportVectorMachines.summary: Cortes and Vapnik published the soft-margin SVM: a classifier that finds the hyperplane with the widest margin between classes.
supportVectorMachines.impact: The default classifier on top of hand-crafted features such as HOG and bags of visual words until 2012.

bilateralFilter.title: The bilateral filter
bilateralFilter.summary: Tomasi and Manduchi smoothed images with weights based on both spatial distance and colour difference, preserving sharp edges.
bilateralFilter.impact: The edge-preserving denoiser inside every photo editor and phone camera pipeline.

condensation.title: CONDENSATION tracking
condensation.summary: Isard and Blake used a particle filter to track object contours through cluttered video.
condensation.impact: Brought probabilistic inference to tracking, the basis of person and object tracking for years.

lenet5.title: LeNet-5 and MNIST
lenet5.summary: Yann LeCun and colleagues trained a convolutional network to read handwritten digits, deployed commercially to process bank cheques.
lenet5.impact: Proof that CNNs worked in real products, more than a decade before the deep learning boom.

sift.title: SIFT
sift.summary: David Lowe introduced local features invariant to scale and rotation, letting the same object be matched across different images.
sift.impact: The backbone of panorama stitching, SLAM and image retrieval throughout the 2000s.

textureSynthesis.title: Efros–Leung texture synthesis
textureSynthesis.summary: Efros and Leung grew new texture from a sample by filling in one pixel at a time from similar neighbourhoods in the source.
textureSynthesis.impact: One of the first non-parametric image generators, the precursor of image quilting and inpainting.

normalizedCuts.title: Normalized cuts
normalizedCuts.summary: Shi and Malik cast segmentation as cutting a graph of pixels, solved with eigenvectors.
normalizedCuts.impact: Grounded graph-based and spectral segmentation in vision.

zhangCalibration.title: Zhang's camera calibration
zhangCalibration.summary: Zhengyou Zhang calibrated a camera from a few photos of a flat checkerboard at different angles.
zhangCalibration.impact: The most widely used calibration method today, built into OpenCV and MATLAB.

multipleViewGeometry.title: Multiple View Geometry (the book)
multipleViewGeometry.summary: Hartley and Zisserman gathered projective geometry, the fundamental matrix, triangulation and bundle adjustment in one book.
multipleViewGeometry.impact: The standard text of 3D vision and the theory beneath structure-from-motion, SLAM and AR.

violaJones.title: Viola–Jones real-time face detection
violaJones.summary: A detector built from Haar features, AdaBoost and a cascade of classifiers, running in real time on the consumer CPUs of the day.
violaJones.impact: Put computer vision into consumer cameras and phones.

graphCuts.title: Energy minimisation with graph cuts
graphCuts.summary: Boykov, Veksler and Zabih solved pixel-labelling problems (segmentation, stereo) quickly with max-flow algorithms.
graphCuts.impact: The engine behind interactive cut-out tools such as GrabCut and many stereo methods.

localBinaryPatterns.title: Local binary patterns (LBP)
localBinaryPatterns.summary: Ojala and colleagues described texture by comparing each pixel with its neighbours, producing a brightness-invariant binary code.
localBinaryPatterns.impact: A light, fast feature widely used in face recognition and surface inspection.

meanShift.title: Mean shift
meanShift.summary: Comaniciu and Meer used mean shift to find density peaks in colour-position space for segmentation and smoothing.
meanShift.impact: Clustering without knowing the number of clusters, used for segmentation and object tracking.

bagOfVisualWords.title: Bag of visual words (Video Google)
bagOfVisualWords.summary: Sivic and Zisserman quantised local features into "visual words" and searched images the way search engines search text.
bagOfVisualWords.impact: The dominant image representation for classification and retrieval for nearly a decade.

poissonEditing.title: Poisson image editing
poissonEditing.summary: Pérez, Gangnet and Blake blended a region seamlessly into another image by solving a Poisson equation on gradients.
poissonEditing.impact: The basis of seamless cloning and object removal in photo editors.

ssim.title: SSIM
ssim.summary: Wang and colleagues measured image quality by structural, luminance and contrast similarity instead of per-pixel error.
ssim.impact: The standard metric for compression, denoising and super-resolution, closer to human perception than PSNR.

hog.title: HOG features
hog.summary: Dalal and Triggs described objects with histograms of oriented gradients and paired them with an SVM to detect pedestrians.
hog.impact: The reference method for object detection throughout the pre-deep-learning era.

pascalVoc.title: PASCAL VOC
pascalVoc.summary: An annual challenge with a shared dataset and evaluation protocol for classification, detection and segmentation.
pascalVoc.impact: Established the field's culture of fair measurement on public benchmarks.

deepAutoencoders.title: Layer-wise pre-trained deep networks
deepAutoencoders.summary: Hinton and Salakhutdinov trained deep networks by pre-training one layer at a time, compressing images far better than PCA.
deepAutoencoders.impact: Showed deep networks could be trained, starting the deep learning wave before GPUs and ImageNet arrived.

surf.title: SURF
surf.summary: Bay, Tuytelaars and Van Gool sped up scale-invariant features with integral images and box filters.
surf.impact: Brought local feature matching to real time, popular in robotics and early AR.

photoTourism.title: Photo Tourism and large-scale SfM
photoTourism.summary: Snavely, Seitz and Szeliski reconstructed 3D scenes and camera positions from thousands of tourist photos on the Internet.
photoTourism.impact: Opened 3D reconstruction from community photos, the forerunner of Photosynth and tools such as COLMAP.

deformablePartModels.title: Deformable part models (DPM)
deformablePartModels.summary: Felzenszwalb and colleagues modelled objects as a root template plus parts that can shift, learned on HOG features.
deformablePartModels.impact: The peak of pre-deep-learning detection, winning PASCAL VOC several years running.

imagenet.title: ImageNet
imagenet.summary: Fei-Fei Li's group built a dataset of over 14 million images labelled along WordNet; the ILSVRC challenge started in 2010.
imagenet.impact: Data at this scale was the precondition for deep learning to show its strength.

kinectPose.title: Human pose estimation on Kinect
kinectPose.summary: Shotton and colleagues used random forests on depth images to recognise body parts in real time.
kinectPose.impact: Put human pose estimation into millions of living rooms and showed the power of synthetic training data.

kittiBenchmark.title: The KITTI benchmark
kittiBenchmark.summary: Geiger, Lenz and Urtasun recorded a real car with stereo cameras, LiDAR and GPS, with benchmarks for stereo, optical flow, odometry and 3D detection.
kittiBenchmark.impact: The first benchmark to put computer vision to work on real-road autonomous driving.

alexnet.title: AlexNet
alexnet.summary: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton trained a convolutional network on GPUs, cutting the ILSVRC 2012 top-5 error from around 26% to 15.3%.
alexnet.impact: The moment the whole field moved to deep learning, after a single competition.

visualizingConvnets.title: Visualising convolutional networks (ZFNet)
visualizingConvnets.summary: Zeiler and Fergus used deconvolutional networks to show what each CNN layer learns, from edges and textures to object parts.
visualizingConvnets.impact: Helped people understand and tune CNNs instead of treating them as black boxes; won ILSVRC 2013.

variationalAutoencoder.title: Variational autoencoders (VAE)
variationalAutoencoder.summary: Kingma and Welling combined neural networks with variational inference to learn a continuous latent space that can be sampled.
variationalAutoencoder.impact: The VAE latent space later became the image compressor inside Stable Diffusion.

rcnn.title: R-CNN
rcnn.summary: Girshick and colleagues combined region proposals with CNN features, sharply improving detection accuracy.
rcnn.impact: The start of the two-stage detector line: Fast R-CNN, then Faster R-CNN.

gan.title: Generative adversarial networks
gan.summary: Goodfellow and colleagues pitted a generator against a discriminator, producing new images that grew steadily more realistic.
gan.impact: Opened generative vision, the groundwork for AI image creation.

microsoftCoco.title: The MS COCO dataset
microsoftCoco.summary: Microsoft COCO offered over 300,000 everyday-scene images with boxes, per-instance masks and sentence captions.
microsoftCoco.impact: Still the standard benchmark for detection, segmentation and image captioning.

deepFace.title: DeepFace
deepFace.summary: Facebook combined 3D face alignment with a deep network, reaching near-human accuracy on LFW.
deepFace.impact: Deep face recognition entered large-scale products, along with the privacy debates that followed.

vggNet.title: VGGNet
vggNet.summary: Simonyan and Zisserman stacked nothing but 3×3 convolutions very deep and placed at the top of ILSVRC 2014.
vggNet.impact: A simple, readable architecture that became the default feature backbone for years.

googLeNet.title: GoogLeNet and the Inception block
googLeNet.summary: Szegedy and colleagues ran convolutions of several sizes in parallel inside Inception blocks and won ILSVRC 2014 with far fewer parameters.
googLeNet.impact: Started the practice of designing architectures for both accuracy and compute cost.

superResolutionCnn.title: SRCNN: super-resolution with a CNN
superResolutionCnn.summary: Dong and colleagues used a small convolutional network to upscale images, beating traditional super-resolution methods.
superResolutionCnn.impact: Started deep image restoration: denoising, deblurring and upscaling on phones.

fullyConvolutionalNetworks.title: Fully convolutional networks (FCN)
fullyConvolutionalNetworks.summary: Long, Shelhamer and Darrell replaced fully connected layers with convolutions to predict a label for every pixel.
fullyConvolutionalNetworks.impact: The template for every semantic segmentation network since.

deepLab.title: DeepLab and atrous convolution
deepLab.summary: Chen and colleagues used dilated (atrous) convolution to widen the receptive field without losing resolution, plus a CRF to sharpen boundaries.
deepLab.impact: The DeepLab line led semantic segmentation for years; atrous convolution became a standard tool.

batchNormalization.title: Batch normalisation
batchNormalization.summary: Ioffe and Szegedy normalised each layer's outputs over a mini-batch, making training much faster and more stable.
batchNormalization.impact: In nearly every CNN since, and a precondition for training very deep networks.

faceNet.title: FaceNet
faceNet.summary: Google learned a face embedding with a triplet loss, where distance reflects how alike two people are.
faceNet.impact: Embedding-based metric learning became the standard approach for face recognition and image retrieval.

fastRcnn.title: Fast R-CNN
fastRcnn.summary: Ross Girshick computed features once per image and pooled them per region with RoI pooling, making inference hundreds of times faster than R-CNN.
fastRcnn.impact: Turned two-stage detection into a single network trained end to end.

flowNet.title: FlowNet
flowNet.summary: Dosovitskiy and colleagues estimated optical flow directly with a CNN trained on the synthetic Flying Chairs data.
flowNet.impact: Moved motion estimation to deep learning, leading to RAFT and later video models.

unet.title: U-Net
unet.summary: An encoder–decoder architecture with skip connections that segments biomedical images accurately from very little training data.
unet.impact: Still the backbone of medical image segmentation, and of diffusion models.

fasterRcnn.title: Faster R-CNN
fasterRcnn.summary: Ren and colleagues added a region proposal network with anchors, so the network proposes its own candidate regions.
fasterRcnn.impact: The classic two-stage detector; anchors and the RPN became core concepts of detection.

yolo.title: YOLO
yolo.summary: Redmon and colleagues treated detection as a single regression over the whole image, reaching real-time speed.
yolo.impact: Opened the way to vision on devices: security cameras, production lines, drones.

neuralStyleTransfer.title: Neural style transfer
neuralStyleTransfer.summary: Gatys, Ecker and Bethge separated content and style using CNN features and repainted photos in the style of a painting.
neuralStyleTransfer.impact: The first time the public saw AI "make" images, launching a wave of artistic photo apps.

dcgan.title: DCGAN
dcgan.summary: Radford and colleagues set out convolutional design rules that made GANs train stably and produce sharp images.
dcgan.impact: Turned GANs from an idea into a usable tool and showed latent spaces have semantic structure.

ssdDetector.title: SSD
ssdDetector.summary: Liu and colleagues detected objects in a single stage on feature maps at several scales.
ssdDetector.impact: With YOLO, shaped fast single-stage detectors widely used on mobile devices.

resnet.title: ResNet
resnet.summary: He and colleagues added residual skip connections, trained networks over 100 layers deep, and won ILSVRC 2015.
resnet.impact: Residual connections became a standard component in almost every deep architecture since.

denseNet.title: DenseNet
denseNet.summary: Huang and colleagues connected each layer to every later layer in a block, reusing features with few parameters.
denseNet.impact: Another take on skip connections, popular in medical imaging for its parameter efficiency.

sortTracking.title: SORT: multi-object tracking
sortTracking.summary: Bewley and colleagues linked detector outputs across frames with a Kalman filter and the Hungarian algorithm, extremely simple and fast.
sortTracking.impact: The "tracking by detection" template behind people counting and traffic monitoring; DeepSORT and ByteTrack grew from it.

cityscapes.title: The Cityscapes dataset
cityscapes.summary: Cordts and colleagues annotated street scenes from 50 cities with fine per-pixel labels.
cityscapes.impact: The standard benchmark for urban scene segmentation and driving.

openPose.title: OpenPose
openPose.summary: Cao and colleagues estimated the skeletons of many people at once using part affinity fields, in real time.
openPose.impact: Its open-source release spread into sports analysis, physiotherapy and animation.

pix2pix.title: pix2pix
pix2pix.summary: Isola and colleagues used a conditional GAN for image-to-image translation: sketches to photos, maps to aerial views, day to night.
pix2pix.impact: One general framework for any paired image-to-image task.

featurePyramidNetworks.title: Feature pyramid networks (FPN)
featurePyramidNetworks.summary: Lin and colleagues merged deep and shallow features along a top-down path, detecting both small and large objects well.
featurePyramidNetworks.impact: A standard part of nearly every modern detector and segmentation model.

maskRcnn.title: Mask R-CNN
maskRcnn.summary: Extended Faster R-CNN with a mask prediction branch, producing per-instance segmentation.
maskRcnn.impact: Unified detection and segmentation in one model, a reference for many industrial applications.

cycleGan.title: CycleGAN
cycleGan.summary: Zhu and colleagues translated images between two domains without paired data, using a cycle-consistency constraint.
cycleGan.impact: Horses to zebras, photos to Monet: domain translation without paired data.

mobileNets.title: MobileNets
mobileNets.summary: Howard and colleagues used depthwise separable convolutions to build small, fast networks for phones and embedded devices.
mobileNets.impact: Put CNNs directly on phones, cameras and IoT devices.

kineticsI3d.title: Kinetics and I3D
kineticsI3d.summary: Carreira and Zisserman introduced the Kinetics action dataset and "inflated" 2D CNNs into 3D for action recognition in video.
kineticsI3d.impact: Grounded deep action recognition, playing the role ImageNet played for still images.

transformerArchitecture.title: The Transformer architecture
transformerArchitecture.summary: The paper Attention Is All You Need dropped recurrence and convolution entirely in favour of self-attention.
transformerArchitecture.impact: Three years later the same architecture displaced CNNs in vision.

focalLoss.title: RetinaNet and focal loss
focalLoss.summary: Lin and colleagues down-weighted easy background examples, letting a single-stage detector beat two-stage accuracy for the first time.
focalLoss.impact: Focal loss became the default for class imbalance in detection.

panopticSegmentation.title: Panoptic segmentation
panopticSegmentation.summary: Kirillov and colleagues unified semantic ("stuff") and instance ("things") segmentation into one task and one metric, PQ.
panopticSegmentation.impact: Redefined the goal of segmentation: every pixel gets both a class and an instance identity.

arcFace.title: ArcFace
arcFace.summary: Deng and colleagues added an angular margin to the softmax loss, producing more discriminative face features.
arcFace.impact: The reference for face recognition in research and in real attendance and verification systems.

yoloV3.title: YOLOv3
yoloV3.summary: Redmon and Farhadi added multi-scale predictions and a Darknet-53 backbone, balancing speed and accuracy well.
yoloV3.impact: For a time the most deployed YOLO, and the start of the community YOLO ecosystem (v4, v5, v8…).

styleGan.title: StyleGAN
styleGan.summary: Karras and colleagues at NVIDIA controlled each level of detail through style vectors, generating faces almost indistinguishable from real ones.
styleGan.impact: The peak of GAN quality, and the start of the deepfake concern.

fcosAnchorFree.title: FCOS: anchor-free detection
fcosAnchorFree.summary: Tian and colleagues predicted each location's distance to the four box sides, dropping anchors entirely.
fcosAnchorFree.impact: Simplified detector design; the anchor-free approach was adopted by later YOLO versions.

efficientNet.title: EfficientNet
efficientNet.summary: Tan and Le scaled depth, width and resolution together with one compound coefficient, on a base network found by architecture search.
efficientNet.impact: High accuracy for far less compute, popular in competitions and real applications.

momentumContrast.title: MoCo: contrastive self-supervised learning
momentumContrast.summary: He and colleagues learned image representations without labels by telling augmentations of one image apart from a queue of others.
momentumContrast.impact: The first time self-supervised features beat supervised pre-training on many detection and segmentation tasks.

simClr.title: SimCLR
simClr.summary: Chen and colleagues showed that strong augmentation, large batches and a projection head bring contrastive learning close to supervised results.
simClr.impact: A simple recipe that made self-supervised learning widespread.

raftFlow.title: RAFT
raftFlow.summary: Teed and Deng estimated optical flow by repeatedly looking up a full all-pairs correlation volume; ECCV 2020 best paper.
raftFlow.impact: The new reference for optical flow, used in frame interpolation and video editing.

nerf.title: NeRF
nerf.summary: Represented a three-dimensional scene as a neural network, synthesising new viewpoints from only a few dozen photos.
nerf.impact: Reshaped 3D vision: a scene became a learnable function rather than a polygon mesh.

detr.title: DETR
detr.summary: Carion and colleagues detected objects with a transformer, removing anchors and the NMS post-processing step.
detr.impact: Detection became set prediction, which simplified the whole pipeline.

denoisingDiffusion.title: Denoising diffusion models (DDPM)
denoisingDiffusion.summary: Ho, Jain and Abbeel generated images by learning to reverse a step-by-step noising process, matching GAN quality.
denoisingDiffusion.impact: The foundation of nearly every image and video generator today.

visionTransformer.title: Vision Transformer (ViT)
visionTransformer.summary: An image is cut into 16×16 patches and fed to a transformer as a sequence of tokens, beating CNNs given enough data.
visionTransformer.impact: Vision and language came to share one architecture, opening the way to multimodal models.

dataEfficientTransformers.title: DeiT
dataEfficientTransformers.summary: Touvron and colleagues trained ViTs on ImageNet-1k alone using distillation and strong augmentation.
dataEfficientTransformers.impact: Showed vision transformers do not require huge private datasets, opening them to the research community.

dallE.title: DALL·E
dallE.summary: OpenAI generated images from text descriptions with an autoregressive transformer over text and image tokens.
dallE.impact: Started the text-to-image era in the public eye.

clip.title: CLIP
clip.summary: Trained on 400 million image–text pairs from the web, classifying unseen classes without labels (zero-shot).
clip.impact: The basis for searching images in natural language and for text-to-image generation.

swinTransformer.title: Swin Transformer
swinTransformer.summary: Liu and colleagues computed attention in shifted windows and built hierarchical features like a CNN.
swinTransformer.impact: A general transformer backbone for detection and segmentation; ICCV 2021 best paper.

dino.title: DINO
dino.summary: Caron and colleagues trained ViTs without labels through self-distillation between teacher and student networks.
dino.impact: Attention maps separated objects from background on their own, starting the DINO line of general visual features.

segFormer.title: SegFormer
segFormer.summary: Xie and colleagues paired a hierarchical transformer encoder with a light MLP decoder for semantic segmentation.
segFormer.impact: Transformer segmentation that is both accurate and light enough to deploy.

maskedAutoencoders.title: Masked autoencoders (MAE)
maskedAutoencoders.summary: He and colleagues masked 75% of image patches at random and trained a ViT to reconstruct them.
maskedAutoencoders.impact: Brought BERT-style "fill in the blanks" pre-training to images, simple and scalable.

convNext.title: ConvNeXt
convNext.summary: Liu and colleagues modernised ResNet step by step with transformer design choices and matched Swin's accuracy.
convNext.impact: Showed pure CNNs still compete when redesigned with modern lessons.

latentDiffusion.title: Latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion
latentDiffusion.summary: Rombach and colleagues ran diffusion in a latent space, cutting compute cost sharply; the model was released publicly in 2022.
latentDiffusion.impact: Text-to-image generation became a mainstream tool that runs on a single consumer GPU.

dallE2.title: DALL·E 2
dallE2.summary: OpenAI generated images with diffusion conditioned on CLIP image embeddings, with a leap in quality and prompt fidelity.
dallE2.impact: Made text-to-image a mass product and started the image-generation race.

imagen.title: Imagen
imagen.summary: Google showed that a large language encoder (T5) improves prompt fidelity more than a bigger image model.
imagen.impact: Established the role of language understanding in image generation, with cascaded multi-resolution diffusion.

laion5b.title: LAION-5B
laion5b.summary: The LAION community released 5.85 billion CLIP-filtered image–text pairs from the web, open for research.
laion5b.impact: Training data for Stable Diffusion and many open models, and a flashpoint in debates over copyright and harmful content.

diffusionTransformers.title: Diffusion transformers (DiT)
diffusionTransformers.summary: Peebles and Xie replaced the U-Net in diffusion models with a transformer whose quality scales steadily with compute.
diffusionTransformers.impact: The backbone of the new generation of image and video generators such as Stable Diffusion 3 and Sora.

blip2.title: BLIP-2
blip2.summary: Salesforce bridged a frozen image encoder and a frozen LLM with a small Q-Former, very cheap to train.
blip2.impact: A recipe for plugging images into LLMs that many later open vision–language models inherited.

controlNet.title: ControlNet
controlNet.summary: Zhang and colleagues added spatial conditions (edges, pose, depth) to a trained diffusion model without damaging it.
controlNet.impact: Turned image generation into a controllable tool for design and content production.

sigLip.title: SigLIP
sigLip.summary: Zhai and colleagues replaced the softmax in CLIP-style training with a pairwise sigmoid loss, more efficient at small batch sizes.
sigLip.impact: The image encoder chosen by many current open vision–language models.

multimodalAssistants.title: Language models that see
multimodalAssistants.summary: Large language models took images as an extra input, answering questions and reasoning about visual content.
multimodalAssistants.impact: Vision moved from a fixed list of labels to open conversation about what an image contains.

groundingDino.title: Grounding DINO
groundingDino.summary: Liu and colleagues combined the DINO detector with language to detect any object described in text.
groundingDino.impact: Detection moved from a fixed label set to an open vocabulary.

segmentAnything.title: Segment Anything (SAM)
segmentAnything.summary: Meta released a promptable segmentation model together with a dataset of over a billion masks.
segmentAnything.impact: The first foundation model for segmentation: usable straight away on unfamiliar images, with no retraining.

dinoV2.title: DINOv2
dinoV2.summary: Meta trained self-supervised on 142 million curated images, producing features that work off the shelf for classification, segmentation and depth.
dinoV2.impact: A general-purpose visual backbone without labels, underpinning many depth and robotics models.

rtDetr.title: RT-DETR
rtDetr.summary: A Baidu team introduced an end-to-end transformer detector that runs in real time: a hybrid encoder processes multi-scale features efficiently, still with no NMS step, and it beat contemporary YOLO models on COCO in both speed and accuracy.
rtDetr.impact: Showed the DETR line was fast enough to deploy, closing the gap between transformers and YOLO in real-time detection.

llava.title: LLaVA
llava.summary: Liu and colleagues fine-tuned an open LLM on image conversations generated by GPT-4, creating an open visual assistant.
llava.impact: Started the wave of open vision–language models the community could train itself.

sdxl.title: SDXL
sdxl.summary: Stability AI released a larger open diffusion model with two text encoders and a refiner, at 1024 px.
sdxl.impact: For a time the most fine-tuned and used open image generator.

gaussianSplatting.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting
gaussianSplatting.summary: Represents a scene as millions of Gaussian primitives, rendering in real time at quality comparable to NeRF.
gaussianSplatting.impact: Brought photo-based 3D reconstruction into real time, fast enough to ship.

dust3r.title: DUSt3R
dust3r.summary: Wang and colleagues predicted 3D point maps directly from a pair of images, with no camera parameters needed.
dust3r.impact: 3D reconstruction moved from a multi-step pipeline to a single network learned end to end.

depthAnything.title: Depth Anything
depthAnything.summary: Yang and colleagues trained monocular depth on tens of millions of unlabelled images pseudo-labelled by a teacher.
depthAnything.impact: Monocular depth that works on any kind of scene, as a foundation model.

yoloWorld.title: YOLO-World
yoloWorld.summary: Cheng and colleagues brought open-vocabulary detection into the YOLO architecture, in real time with text prompts.
yoloWorld.impact: Made open-vocabulary detection fast enough for edge devices.

stableDiffusion3.title: Stable Diffusion 3 and rectified flow
stableDiffusion3.summary: Esser and colleagues combined rectified flow with a multimodal transformer (MMDiT), clearly improving text rendering and prompt fidelity.
stableDiffusion3.impact: Rectified flow and MMDiT became the recipe of many new image generators.

videoGeneration.title: Video generation
videoGeneration.summary: Diffusion models extended into the time dimension, producing short videos with coherent motion.
videoGeneration.impact: The field's new challenge: temporal consistency and an understanding of scene physics.

yoloV10.title: YOLOv10
yoloV10.summary: Wang and colleagues trained YOLO with dual label assignments to remove NMS, moving towards end-to-end real-time detection.
yoloV10.impact: The YOLO line adopted DETR's NMS-free idea, cutting deployment latency.

segmentAnything2.title: SAM 2
segmentAnything2.summary: Meta extended Segment Anything to video with a streaming memory, segmenting and tracking objects across frames.
segmentAnything2.impact: One foundation model for both image and video segmentation.

vggt.title: VGGT
vggt.summary: Wang and colleagues (Oxford, Meta) predicted cameras, depth, point maps and point tracks from one to hundreds of images in a single forward pass; CVPR 2025 best paper.
vggt.impact: A foundation model for 3D geometry that replaces most of the traditional SfM pipeline.

dinoV3.title: DINOv3
dinoV3.summary: Meta scaled self-supervised learning to a 7-billion-parameter model and 1.7 billion images, giving high-quality dense features, satellite imagery included.
dinoV3.impact: Label-free visual features that beat many specialised models on detection, segmentation and depth.

openVisionLanguage.title: Open vision–language models and embodied vision
openVisionLanguage.summary: Many open-weight vision–language models were released that run on personal machines and edge devices, while vision for robots and agents became a main research direction.
openVisionLanguage.impact: This part of the history is still being written. Tell us which milestones this page should add.

segmentAnything3.title: SAM 3
segmentAnything3.summary: Meta segmented and tracked every instance matching a concept given as text or an example image, instead of a single click.
segmentAnything3.impact: Segmentation moved from "this object" to "every object of this kind", unifying detection, segmentation and tracking.
